member.summary: Enumeration with the different types to which a function is assigned in the external communication protocol.This value can be used to check from which protocol version the respective function is available, so that a distinction can be made within the program flow.e.g.introduction of the EOT\r\n command at the end of each data transmission.

member.name: F:BiometraLibrary.DeviceExtComClasses.DeviceComClasses.EnExtComProtFunctions.FUNCTION_EOT_CMD
member.summary: Enumeration value for the assignment of the protocol version from which an EOT\r\n is sent by the device at the end of each data transmission. The EOT command was introduced so that a general end of the data transmission can be recognized, from which all requested commands were answered by the device, without checking the content of the data already during the reception.

member.name: F:BiometraLibrary.DeviceExtComClasses.DeviceComClasses.EnExtComProtFunctions.FUNCTION_SPRG_PROG_NUM_DEZ
member.summary: Enumeration value for the assignment of the protocol version, from which the program number in the SPRG command can be transferred as a decimal numerical value. The format was adapted, since the remaining commands already expect decimal numerical values.

member.name: F:BiometraLibrary.DeviceExtComClasses.DeviceComClasses.EnExtComProtFunctions.FUNCTION_PPRT_OVERVIEW_COMMA_SEPARATOR_BLOCK_NUM
member.summary: Enumeration value for assigning the protocol version, as of which a comma is used as separator between the individual parameters instead of a space when executing the PPRT command for reading out the overview of all RunLogFiles available on the device. The output was adjusted because individual parameters within the runlog overview may use a space character and thus a split based on the space character results in more parameters than actually exist in the data set. Furthermore, the output was extended in such a way that the block number is transferred at the end of the data.

member.name: F:BiometraLibrary.DeviceExtComClasses.DeviceComClasses.EnExtComProtFunctions.FUNCTION_TCDA_GET_ACT_BLOCK_PROG_COMMA_SEPARATOR
member.summary: Enumeration value for the assignment of the protocol version, from which a comma is used as separator between the individual parameters instead of a blank character when executing the TCDA 14 command with which the current block program is read out. The output was adjusted because individual parameters within the current program may use a space character and thus a split based on the space character results in more parameters than actually exist in the data set.

member.name: F:BiometraLibrary.DeviceExtComClasses.DeviceComClasses.EnExtComProtFunctions.FUNCTION_RPRG_RTPL_NUM_OF_ENTRIES_IF_ZERO
member.summary: Enumeration value for assigning the protocol version from which the number of available programs/templates is also sent when executing the RPRG or the RTPL command if none are available. In this case 0 is then transmitted. With older protocol versions only RPRG or RTPL is sent as completion identifier without the 0 as identifier that no programs/templates are available.

member.name: F:BiometraLibrary.DeviceExtComClasses.DeviceComClasses.EnExtComProtFunctions.FUNCTION_VALID_DEFAULT_SAVE_DATE_RTPL
member.summary: Enumeration value for assigning the protocol version from which the polymerase templates specified on the device, which are available directly after a factory reset, have a valid storage date when the RTPL command is executed. With older protocol versions, the memory date 00.00.00 was output in the standard template, which is invalid. As of the corresponding protocol version, 01.01.2000 is output.

member.summary: Within this class an object is described in which the hold time of a program step is mapped.For the initialization of the value there is no limitation. Only with the method AddTimeSpan a limitation on the maximum time value takes place, so that for the computation of the program run time on the ME and the application software an identical limit is used, which is conditioned by the RE

member.summary: Maximum hold time that can be set when adding a TimeSpan by the AddTimeSpan method. The limitation of the calculated hold time results from the limitation of the number of passes of a step within the RE. Due to the fact that the number of steps within the RE is limited to short.MaxValue, this limit must be used when adding a time increment so that the runtime calculation between the ME and this application software has the same limit

member.name: M:BiometraLibrary.HelperClasses.BackgroundHelperClasses.BackgroundTimerWorker.#ctor(System.Double,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Constructor to initialize the timed background processing based on the passed time interval.Based on this time interval, the background processing will be called cyclically after it has been started until the background processing is stopped.If the passed flag is true, the background processing will be called even if the device is in sleep mode.If the function to wake up from background processing is not yet available, the cyclic background processing will be initialized automatically, which cannot be used in sleep mode.
member.param: Time interval [ms] used to set the interval at which background processing is to be executed cyclically.
true --> background processing is also executed when the device is in sleep mode. false --> background processing is not executed when the device is in sleep mode.
member.exception: Exception thrown if the passed time interval is not in the valid range (greater than 0 and less than or equal to Int32.MaxValue)
